input.text: Your summing loop is skipping part of the list. When you add up a collection, think about which index you should start at so that every element gets counted exactly once — including the very first one.

content.text: Your loop currently leaves out the first number in the input, which is why every result is too small (and a single number gives 0). Make sure your loop visits the whole list from the beginning.

input.text: Your loop starts counting at 1, which means the element at position zero is skipped. Python list positions begin at zero, so to include every element you need the loop to start at zero rather than one. The single-number case makes this obvious: with one number, starting at 1 means the loop body never runs, leaving the total at zero.

content.text: Your loop begins at index 1, but Python indexing starts at 0, so the first element is skipped. Change the loop's starting point to zero so every element is included.
